idiom_name: step value + thunk + single driver loop, with done/more combinators
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: define a closed step type with two cases - a finished value and a suspended thunk returning the next step - and rewrite every function of the mutually recursive group to return that type instead of calling its partners. A single driver loop keeps invoking the returned thunk until a finished step appears, then returns its value. Keep thunk construction in small combinators (done/more or tailcall/result) so call sites stay readable, and never call the algorithms or the driver from inside a step. Convert the whole group: one unconverted call is enough to make the stack grow again.
pitfalls: Leaving one call in the group direct: the stack grows again at exactly that edge and the defect only shows on deep inputs.
Calling the driver from inside a step, or creating one driver per call, which adds frames instead of replacing them.
Assuming stack safety is memory safety: an unbounded number of steps still exhausts the heap when the recursion does not terminate.

Closure allocation per step: each suspended thunk usually allocates a new closure on the heap; at millions-of-steps scale this can cause GC pauses or memory pressure that a native stack frame would not.

Non-tail flatMap in free monad chains: appending a trailing map after a recursive bind shifts the recursion off the tail position, degrading space complexity from O(1) to O(N) and causing OutOfMemoryError on deep inputs.

Broken stack traces: the driver loop replaces the logical call chain with a flat iteration; debugging must rely on step-context carried in the thunk or in the step value, not on the native stack trace.

Wrong move: converting branching (non-tail) recursion into a trampoline by building deferred continuations at each branch point -> the continuation chain accumulates on the heap exactly as frames did on the stack, so memory still grows with depth and the overflow merely changes venue -> instead trampoline only tail-recursive or mutually recursive shapes and keep an explicit stack data structure for branching traversals.

Wrong move: deferring each step with setTimeout, queueMicrotask or Promise callbacks in JavaScript to escape the stack limit -> the logical call chain dissolves into the event loop, exceptions no longer reach the original caller and synchronous code observes unfinished results -> instead run the driver loop synchronously and reserve async scheduling for work that is genuinely asynchronous.

Wrong move: relying on try/finally or exception unwinding across a trampolined group -> suspended thunks never actually call their partners, so catch and cleanup blocks fire at the driver's unwind point instead of the logical call site -> instead propagate errors as values inside done steps (Result/Either) and place resource scopes explicitly around the driver.
